intro: When a KiwiSaver member can take savings out to buy a first home, what can be withdrawn, and how much has to stay in the account.
explanation:
## What the rule allows

A KiwiSaver member who is buying a first home may be able to withdraw savings from the account to help pay for it. It is meant for first-time buyers. The advice from Inland Revenue (IRD) is to speak to both the provider and Kāinga Ora - Homes and Communities before going ahead, and it notes that some funds do not permit these withdrawals.

## How long a member must have been in KiwiSaver

The member must have been in KiwiSaver, or in an eligible fund, for the minimum period shown on this page before a first-home withdrawal can be made.

## What can be withdrawn and what must stay

Five kinds of money can be taken out:

- the member's own contributions
- the employer's contributions
- the government contribution
- interest earned on the account
- any fee subsidies the member received

Not everything is available. Savings that were transferred in from an Australian complying superannuation scheme are excluded. A set amount, shown on this page, also has to stay in the account.

## If the buyer has owned a home before

Owning a home in the past does not always close the door. Savings may still be usable for a later purchase, and the provider can send the member to Kāinga Ora, which assesses whether their position matches that of a first-home buyer.

## Supporting an application

IRD's myIR service can produce a PDF showing a member's income and KiwiSaver deductions, which can be printed or saved and used to support an application made through Kāinga Ora.
